title: Honda 1.5L turbo (2016-18 Civic, 2017-18 CR-V): oil level rising, misfire codes, oil dilution
summary: Fuel diluting the oil on short cold-weather trips can raise the oil level and set P0300-P0304 or P0172. Honda's product update is PCM (PGM-FI) and transmission software plus an A/C control unit update and an oil change; the 2017-18 CR-V also got a 6-year, unlimited-mileage powertrain extension for resulting damage.

specs.name: CR-V service bulletins
specs.value: 18-114 (software update with A/C control unit) and 18-124 (software update only)

specs.name: A/C control unit, from February 1, 2019
specs.value: Reflash it; replacing it is no longer the procedure

specs.name: CR-V powertrain warranty extension (bulletin 19-037, campaign X4A)
specs.value: From 5 years / 60,000 miles to 6 years, unlimited miles, from original sale date

specs.name: Extension covers
specs.value: Engine parts damaged by these concerns, such as camshafts, rocker arm assemblies and spark plugs

specs.name: Campaign states (final scope)
specs.value: AK, CT, IL, IN, IA, ME, MA, MI, MN, MT, NE, NH, NJ, NY, ND, OH, PA, RI, SD, VT, WI

steps.text: Typical complaint: oil level above the full mark, MIL on, lack of power or misfire, worst on very short drives in cold weather.
Check the VIN for the open product update. Vehicles outside the campaign states get normal diagnosis, and if the problem is confirmed the update is done under normal warranty.

Product update (18-114 / 18-137, as revised): update the A/C control unit, reset the maintenance minder, change the engine oil (the filter doesn't need changing), clear DTCs, and update PGM-FI and TCU software to the latest version.
Then reset the throttle position learned values and do the PCM idle learn.
On a 2017-18 CR-V with misfire, P0172, or a whirling noise from the engine, damage to camshafts, rocker arms or spark plugs is covered under the 6-year extension.

body:
The CR-V campaign started in five states (Maine, Minnesota, North Dakota, South Dakota, Wisconsin) in October 2018, grew to 21 cold-weather states in December 2018, and was extended to the 2016-18 Civic on December 21, 2018.

The Civic match leaves out the Type R. Not every 2016-18 Civic has the 1.5L turbo; check the engine.
